issues.description: The template Lecture.java provides a constructor with only three parameters (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents), but the problem statement and UML require a constructor that initializes all five attributes (lectureName, numberOfInscribedStudents, numberOfGuestStudents, numberOfLecturers, numberOfTutors). The solution implements a five-parameter constructor. This mismatch can confuse students about the required constructor signature and the order of parameters.
issues.suggestedFix: Modify the template Lecture.java to either remove the incorrect three-parameter constructor or replace it with the five-parameter constructor matching the UML and problem description: public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors) { ... } ensuring the parameter order matches the UML. Keep a TODO in the constructor body if the intention is for students to implement it.
